<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **33** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ac33a57dfa5e788fca8d032af72dd8b9d158d35` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fa63e1056a702db9e7ccffc8306a7c0fa919fbd3` — the merge of head `a48f373a291779626fff06ab247c279f5719ff29` into base `6ac33a57dfa5e788fca8d032af72dd8b9d158d35`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fa63e1056a702db9e7ccffc8306a7c0fa919fbd3 && git checkout fa63e1056a702db9e7ccffc8306a7c0fa919fbd3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6ac33a57dfa5e788fca8d032af72dd8b9d158d35 a48f373a291779626fff06ab247c279f5719ff29 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6ac33a57dfa5e788fca8d032af72dd8b9d158d35 && git merge --no-ff a48f373a291779626fff06ab247c279f5719ff29

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ac33a57dfa5e788fca8d032af72dd8b9d158d35
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6ac33a57dfa5e788fca8d032af72dd8b9d158d35` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a48f373a291779626fff06ab247c279f5719ff29`

### ① Derived judgments

- **The move is byte-faithful. Correct.** I diffed the four removed `rest-server.ts` list blocks against `createMetaListReadGate` (the new tail of `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`).
  - **App arm:**
    - the same `ctx?.userId` guard;
    - the same `resolveRegisteredServices(serviceProbe(ctx), items)`, where `sources.serviceProbe` is `serviceProbeFor(caller.__kernel)`, the deleted delegate's body;
    - the same once-per-list `resolveNavServability`/`resolveNavDocAudience`, over a superset of the ports the delegates built.
  - **Dashboard arm:** it still runs for an anonymous caller and fails open on a null probe, as before.
  - **Book and doc arms:** `resolveDocsAudience(sources, …)` and `fetchAudienceBooks(sources)` are exactly what `RestServer.resolveDocsAudience` and `fetchAudienceBooks` delegated to.
  - **Reading `visible` instead of `items`** is equivalent for `app`: the only earlier mutation is the `api`-only served-set face.
  - **Order:** the gate sits where the app filter sat, before `?id=` (app-only) and before the locale collapse, slim and mask. Dashboard, book and doc moved ahead of `?id=`/`?object=`, which are type-disjoint, so every set is unchanged.
  - **Rewrap:** the `judged !== list` rewrap is wire-identical to the old unconditional rewrap.
  - **Unchanged:** `?preview=draft`, anonymous and fault handling (`rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable` via `metaReadAudienceSources.resolveCaller`).
  - The `rest.test.ts` list-route tests are untouched: `it()` 215→215, `expect(` 490→490.
- **The 83 retargeted sites. Correct.**
  - The removed `rest.DELEGATE(` occurrences across the three files are 75 `filterAppForUser` + 4 `filterDashboardForUser` + 3 `resolveRegisteredServices` + 1 `resolveNavServability` = 83, with zero leftovers on the branch.
  - `it()` 215/16/18 and `expect(` 490/25/42 are unchanged.
  - Each retarget reproduces the deleted one-liner: `resolveRegisteredServices(rest.serviceProbeFor(kernel), …)`, and `gateOf` → `resolveNavServability({...rest.metaListSource(p), navPruneLogged: rest.navPruneLogged})`.
  - The delegates carried no guard of their own, so no path weakened.
- **The dispatcher rows. Correct.**
  - Every exit now passes through `gateMetaListAnswer` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`): the gate, then `maskObjectSchemaList`, outside the lookups' swallowing `try`s. The exits are protocol, `MetadataService.list` and the ObjectQL registry (`getAllObjects`/`listItems`).
  - The registry `objects` exit hands the raw `typeOrName` to the mask. `maskObjectSchemaList` folds it via `pluralToSingular`, so it stays masked.
  - The parity pin (`meta-list-read-gate-parity.test.ts`, 40 cases) holds status, code and item shape equal for holder and non-holder, over doc?include=content, doc, docs, book, books, app, apps, dashboard, object, objects and view, plus the two fallback exits.
  - The composed-host pin (`hono-meta-list-read-gate.conformance.test.ts`, 6 cases) drives the card's three rows through the real `createHonoApp`.
  - Anonymous: the dispatcher answers 401 before any read, on both sides of the fix (see ③ b).
- **Deviation 4 is the declared fail-closed posture, not a regression.**
  - **Hosts that reach the branch:** `createHonoApp` (`packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts:301`, `new HttpDispatcher(kernel)` + the catch-all) and any adapter on `HttpDispatcher`. On `createDispatcherPlugin` hosts (cli `serve`, plugin-dev, `packages/verify`), `RestServer` answers `/meta`.
  - **Every in-repo kernel composition** registers `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` as `protocol`: either `ObjectQLPlugin`, whose `registerProtocol` defaults to true (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:250,295,479`), or `MetadataProtocolPlugin` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/plugin.ts:256`). That implementation has `getMetaItems` (`protocol.ts:7409`). So no shipped host serves a plain doc list from the `MetadataService` fallback.
  - **The "no `getMetaItems`" fault** needs a user-composed kernel without ObjectQL. On such a kernel, `/meta/doc/:name` has faulted identically since #20236 (the same `listMetaItems` port, so `readMetaList` throws).
  - **The other change closes a real hole:** a thrown mask fault on the protocol exit used to fall through to the `MetadataService` exit and serve objects unmasked, which ADR-0106 D6 tier 3 forbids.
  - Both are in the PR body's Acceptance notes, and both match #20129's precedent.
- **No second resolver. Correct.** The runtime's `metaItemReadGateSources` supplies only `resolveCaller` (the dispatch-resolved `executionContext`), `resolveSecurityService`, `listMetaItems`, `serviceProbe` and `navPruneLogged`. `gateMetaListAnswer` unwraps, rewraps and maps faults; it decides nothing.
- **Deviation 2 is an acceptable wart.**
  - `export { filterAppForUser } from './meta-item-read-gate.js'` sits at `rest-server.ts:189`. `index.ts` names its exports one by one (no `export *`), and the package has only the `.` subpath, so the re-export is not public.
  - ADR-0056 row 18 (`docs/adr/0056-…md:70`) is Tier H. The PR body and the os-dev report note it for the maintainer.
  - Recommendation: the seat carries the re-anchor as a row in its next Tier-H batch, so the bridge does not rot. Not a required change.
- **The census arithmetic is right.**
  - `this.resolveExecCtx(` 68→66, mentions 92→90, same-line `.catch(` 15→13. So CAUGHT goes 23→21, with 8 continuation sites and 45 bare sites unchanged.
  - The two removed sites are exactly the app and dashboard blocks' same-line caught calls.
  - The inline floor `>=12` sits against a population of 13.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes`, `@objectstack/rest` `minor`, `@objectstack/runtime` `patch`, with no arm.
- The one new value export, `createMetaListReadGate`, exists on the barrel (`packages/rest/src/index.ts:89`). The changeset (`.changeset/20237-dispatcher-meta-list-gate.md`), the PR body and claim `5859027544` agree.
- Deviation 4 narrows no accept set. The requests accepted are unchanged; only the outputs move. They are either pruned to the declared contract (ADR-0046 §6.7, `apps.mdx`), or a fault where a gate input could not be read, which is the same posture #20236 landed as `patch`.
- So `(narrowing)` + BREAKING is not owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Surface:** 11 files, 1086/352 lines, all inside the claim's file surface: the gate module, `rest-server.ts`, `index.ts`, runtime `meta.ts`, the rest and runtime tests, one http-conformance pin, the census test and one changeset. No governed path, and no `packages/spec` or `metadata-core` edit.
- **PR body vs diff:** every checkable claim holds: the 83 sites, the `it()` counts, the census numbers, the mask per transport, the three exits gated, and the re-export off the barrel. `Fixes #20237` is the only closing keyword.
- **CI on `a48f373a2`:** 32 check runs: 23 success, 3 expected skips (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), 6 in progress (Lint & Repo Gates; Test Core 2/4/5; Type Check workspace and consumer gates), 0 failed. The required set is not yet green, and nothing is red.
- **Out-of-scope (a): confirmed at source.**
  - The dispatcher list branch reads only `query.package` and `query.preview`.
  - `slimDocList` compares the raw segment (`type !== 'doc'`), so `/meta/docs` without `?include=content` serves bodies.
  - `?id=` and `?object=` are never read.
  - `RestServer` honours all three: the #7566 block, the view switcher, and the `metaTypeSingular`-folded slim.
  These are projections only, and nothing gated leaks. Not this PR's change.
- **Out-of-scope (b): confirmed at source.**
  - `handleMetadataRequest` opens with `shouldDenyAnonymous({userId, isSystem})`, with no path or method, which returns true for any unauthenticated caller (`packages/core/src/security/anonymous-deny.ts:152`).
  - `RestServer`'s umbrella gate grants anonymous callers reachability of book and doc GETs via `isPublicAudienceRead` (`rest-server.ts:2752`), and §6.7 admits `public` only.
  - So the dispatcher is stricter: it withholds and exposes nothing. Not this PR's change.
